tests.result: Swift helper uses production ProjectLibraryFileStore.save with bounded valid prior/candidate fixtures and unrestricted controls. Verification decodes complete snapshots, compares exact bytes and checks active identity plus both unrelated archived/open records. The rename driver chooses strict prior versus candidate verification based on a witnessed exact-target rename boundary.

Recorded EFBIG run passed with RLIMIT_FSIZE=32768, prior=3900 bytes, candidate=242569 bytes, application limit=8388608. NSCocoaErrorDomain 512 alone is not treated as proof; captured errno immediately after save is 27 (EFBIG), reset before save. All phases exit 0; save threw; fresh process reopened prior.

Before-rename witness is renameat before-call, realRenameCalled=false, child PID 3077 observed SIGSTOP then owned SIGKILL with return -9. Fully staged candidate bytes match; target at hook and after interruption match prior.

After-rename witness is renameat after-success, realRenameCalled=true and realReturnCode=0, child PID 3081 observed SIGSTOP then owned SIGKILL with return -9. Target at hook and fresh-process reopened result match complete candidate. Prior-equality flags correctly remain false.
Rename-eio witness is renameat rejected, realRenameCalled=false, errno 5. Save returned caught error and fresh-process reopened exact prior. Unrestricted controls reopen candidate in all scenarios.

Recomputed all 20 recorded fixture/file SHA256 values and lengths across EFBIG and three rename scenarios; zero mismatches. Compared after/library/control bytes, JSON active IDs and all unrelated records independently: every expected comparison true. Before staged-at-hook equals candidate, before at-hook equals prior, after at-hook equals candidate.
